questions.title: Defining the Michaelis constant
questions.question: Which of the following descriptions best defines the Michaelis Menten constant?

options.A: The substrate concentration at half Vmax
options.B: The maximum velocity of the chemical reaction
options.C: The minimum energy required for the reaction
options.D: The inhibitor concentration exactly at the Vmax

explanations.A: Correct. As substrate concentration increases, reaction velocity rises toward a maximum, Vmax, at which the enzyme is saturated. The substrate concentration that produces half of that maximal velocity is termed the Michaelis constant, Km — a smaller Km reflects higher enzyme-substrate affinity, and Km is used to compare the catalytic efficiency of different enzymes for their substrates.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Vmax itself is the maximum reaction velocity, a separate quantity from Km, which is a substrate concentration, not a velocity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for a reaction to proceed, an unrelated quantity to Km.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Km is defined for the uninhibited reaction; an inhibitor concentration at some reference velocity is not what the Michaelis constant measures, even though a competitive inhibitor does raise the APPARENT Km.

questions.learning_objective: Define Km as the substrate concentration producing half of Vmax.
